sections.title: What Flu Vaccinations Are
sections.proseHtml:
Seasonal flu vaccination helps reduce the risk of catching flu and can lessen illness if you do become unwell.

Many people consider a flu vaccination each year as part of sensible winter health planning.

Flu vaccination offers a straightforward way to reduce seasonal flu risk with clear guidance on next steps.

Flu vaccination helps your immune system recognise flu viruses. It reduces the likelihood and severity of flu for many people.

sections.title: Who Should Consider Flu Vaccinations
sections.proseHtml:
Why Flu Vaccination Matters Flu can cause significant illness during winter months. Vaccination is a practical way to reduce risk for many people. Seasonal protection Individual suitability When to contact the pharmacy Emergency signs to know

Understanding Suitability Not everyone can receive a flu vaccination in every setting. Suitability depends on your health, medicines and current circumstances. Individual assessment Medicines and allergies Current symptoms Contact the pharmacy to confirm

Getting The Right Care Flu vaccination is one part of winter health planning. The pharmacy can advise on suitability and guide you when other care is more appropriate. Suitability check Clear next steps Aftercare guidance Emergency guidance

sections.title: Eligibility and suitability
sections.proseHtml:
Who Can Use This Service

Suitability for flu vaccination is confirmed individually. Contact the pharmacy to check whether vaccination is appropriate for you.

  • Individual assessment
  • Medicines and allergy review
  • Current health status
  • Contact the pharmacy to confirm

Is This Right For Me

If you are unsure whether flu vaccination is suitable, contact the pharmacy for guidance.

  • Share relevant health information
  • Ask about suitability
  • Alternative care guidance when needed
  • Emergency advice when needed

Before you contact the pharmacy

Having basic health information ready can help the pharmacy advise you.

  • Medicines list
  • Allergy history
  • Recent health notes
  • Questions you want to ask

Checking Suitability

Contact the pharmacy if unsure — they can advise on the best pathway for your situation.

  • Phone enquiry
  • Scope explained
  • Alternative care guidance
  • Guidance on next steps

sections.title: What happens during the consultation
sections.proseHtml:
1. How The Service Works Contact the pharmacy to confirm how flu vaccination is arranged locally. If suitable, you receive assessment and vaccination with clear advice on next steps. Contact the pharmacy Suitability check
  2. Assessment Steps The assessment covers relevant health information, confirms suitability and explains the vaccination process before proceeding. Health information review Suitability confirmed
  3. The Vaccination Process Where suitable, vaccination is given with clear aftercare guidance and advice on when to seek further help. Suitability confirmed Vaccination given
  4. During your visit Allow time to ask questions and receive clear aftercare guidance. Questions encouraged Clear explanation

sections.title: Preparing For Your Visit
sections.proseHtml:
Preparing For Your Visit

Bring a medicines list, notes about allergies and any questions you want to ask.

  • Medicines list
  • Allergy information
  • Questions to ask
  • Loose clothing for upper arm access

sections.title: Safety Considerations
sections.proseHtml:
Safety Considerations Flu vaccination is not suitable for everyone. Care falls outside pharmacy scope when symptoms suggest urgent medical review is needed. Individual suitability Emergency guidance Not for emergency presentations Clinical limits apply

When To Seek GP Or Urgent Care Severe, persistent or worsening symptoms and emergency presentations need medical review beyond routine vaccination. Chest pain or breathing difficulty Severe allergic reaction Sudden neurological symptoms Feeling seriously unwell

After Vaccination Most people tolerate flu vaccination well. Follow aftercare advice and report any unexpected reactions promptly. Common mild reactions When to seek help Report concerns promptly Keep a note of vaccination date

faqs.question: Do I need a consultation for flu vaccinations?
faqs.answer: Contact the pharmacy to confirm how the service is currently arranged.

faqs.question: What applies locally for flu vaccinations?
faqs.answer: Local arrangements can vary — contact the pharmacy to confirm what applies where you live.

faqs.question: What should I bring to my flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Bring a medicines list, allergy information and any questions you want to ask about the service.

faqs.question: Who can have a flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Suitability is checked individually. Contact the pharmacy to confirm whether vaccination is appropriate for you.

faqs.question: Can I speak to someone before arranging a flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Yes — contact the pharmacy to discuss suitability and how the service is arranged.

faqs.question: What if flu vaccination is not suitable for me?
faqs.answer: You receive guidance on appropriate next steps, which may include advice on other care when needed.

faqs.question: What happens during flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: Relevant health information is reviewed, suitability is confirmed, and vaccination is given where appropriate, with aftercare advice.

faqs.question: When should I see a GP instead of having a flu vaccination?
faqs.answer: If you have severe or worsening symptoms, or feel seriously unwell, seek GP or urgent care rather than routine vaccination.
